articles.description:
Hey Dev Community! 👋
I’ve been working on a project where I combined Three.js with React to create an interactive 3D experience. This is something I’m really excited to share, and I’d love to get some feedback and tips from all of you!
The Project: Schildr
The project is built for schildr.com, with a focus on the Configure Yourself section, where users can interact with 3D visualizations.

What is Schildr?
Schildr is a platform that lets you customize and configure products in a 3D space, and I had the chance to take part in building the 3D visualization component of the experience. The goal was to make the customization process not only functional but also visually engaging, and that’s where Three.js comes in.
The Tech Stack
React: To build the front-end and handle state management.
Three.js: For creating the 3D scenes, rendering, and adding interactive elements.
React-Three-Fiber: A powerful React renderer for Three.js, which made the integration smooth and helped me manage 3D scenes directly within the React component tree.
Styled Components: To handle the CSS styling for the React components.
Key Features
3D Product Customization


Smooth Animations


Optimized for Performance



Challenges & Solutions
Managing 3D Scene in React
Performance Tuning

Why Three.js + React?
The combination of Three.js and React is incredibly powerful for building interactive and visually rich user interfaces. React provides a solid structure for managing the UI, while Three.js gives you the flexibility to create detailed and engaging 3D content. By using React-Three-Fiber, the two technologies work together like a charm, and the experience is super responsive.
Check It Out!
Feel free to explore the project at https://schildr.com and take a look at the Configure Yourself section for the full experience. If you have any suggestions or feedback, I’d love to hear it!
articles.title: Building an Interactive 3D Experience with Three.js and React for Schildr

articles.description:
In Week 5 of my Open Source Development course, the task was to add a new feature to another student’s repository. I decided to work on the project Repository-Context-Packager. This tool helps package useful information about a repository so it can be used later.
Right now, to run the tool you need to type a long command every time. For example:
repo-packager "PATH/TO/REPO" \
  --output "output.txt" \
  --include "*.js" \
  --exclude "*test*" \
  --max-file-size 1024 \
  --format "json"

If you always use the same options, typing this again and again is not very user-friendly.
To fix this, I added support for a TOML config file. This means you can create a simple file called .repo-packager-config.toml in your project folder:
output = "output.txt"
include = "*.js"
exclude = "*test*"
max_fil…
articles.title: Adding TOML Config File Support to an Open Source CLI Project

articles.author: Nate Patel
articles.description:
Introduction
As Nate Patel, a technology leader with over 20 years of experience in AI, product, and engineering, often highlights, governance is not just about compliance. It’s about building responsible AI systems that create long-term value, minimize risk, and earn stakeholder trust. His perspectives emphasize that ethical AI is fast becoming a business necessity, not an optional add-on.
Why Ethical AI Matters
By 2025, nearly 65% of enterprises rank AI governance as their top compliance challenge, while 72% of consumers report they are more likely to trust companies that openly communicate about their AI practices.
Here’s a simple comparison:
Key Governance Frameworks Every Business Should Know
1. Responsible AI Pillars Model
Focuses on fairness, accountability, transparency, and human oversight. These pillars serve as the foundation for any governance plan.
2. Trustworthy AI Lifecycle Framework
Outlines governance across the AI lifecycle:
Data Collection → Bias Checks → Model Training → Governance Review → Human Oversight → Continuous Monitoring
3. Compliance-by-Design Model
Integrates governance checkpoints directly into product development, ensuring AI systems meet regulatory requirements before launch.
4. Adaptive Governance Framework
Recognizes that AI and regulations evolve rapidly, so businesses need flexible structures that can adapt without slowing innovation.
Ethical AI in Practice: Industry Comparisons
Read More: The Rise of Ethical AI: Governance Frameworks Every Business Should Know
articles.title: The Rise of Ethical AI: Governance Frameworks Every Business Should Know
